decision_reason: A1 already distinguishes most unseen pairs through posture, impact, intensity and temporal structure. Jumping has the weakest seen coverage and is close to descending stairs; bilateral leg coordination adds a physically independent contrast transferable from running and rowing. Preserve the remaining concepts rather than introduce uncertain elevator-travel, stair-direction or equipment-specific attributes. Standing and standing in an elevator still may remain indistinguishable during stationary or constant-speed intervals.

attributes.name: motion_intensity
attributes.definition: Overall magnitude and energy of motion within a window, including both linear and rotational components.

attributes.name: cadence
attributes.definition: Rate at which a meaningful periodic motion unit repeats over time. Cadence measures repetitions per unit time, not the total number of repetitions in the recording.

levels.Low: No clear periodic repetition or a slow repetition rate.

attributes.name: smoothness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion changes continuously rather than through sustained rapid fluctuations.

levels.Medium: Moderately smooth motion with some fluctuations.
levels.High: Continuous and smooth motion with little fluctuation.

attributes.name: impulsiveness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion contains short, abrupt, high-magnitude changes or impacts.

levels.Low: Few or no pronounced abrupt peaks.

attributes.name: posture_inclination
attributes.definition: Average gravity-relative inclination of the global load-bearing body configuration within a window, rather than the orientation of an isolated moving limb.

levels.High: Strongly inclined or nearly horizontal relative to gravity.

attributes.name: posture_variability
attributes.definition: Extent to which the global load-bearing body configuration changes relative to gravity within a window, rather than local limb-orientation changes.

attributes.name: rotational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of angular or rotational motion during the activity.

attributes.name: translational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of sustained linear progression or locomotor translation within a window.

levels.High: Prominent sustained translational or locomotor motion.

attributes.name: motion_regularity
attributes.definition: Temporal consistency and predictability of the motion pattern.

levels.Low: Irregular and poorly predictable motion pattern.
levels.Medium: Partly structured motion with moderate variability.

attributes.name: bilateral_leg_synchrony
attributes.definition: Degree to which substantial movements of the left and right legs occur together in time rather than alternately or independently. Static bilateral similarity does not constitute synchronous movement.

levels.Low: Little substantial simultaneous leg movement; movement is absent, predominantly alternating or independent.
levels.Medium: Substantial leg movements are intermittently simultaneous or show mixed coordination.
levels.High: Substantial leg movements are predominantly simultaneous.

operations.reason: motion_intensity: G3 supports overall acceleration and rotation magnitude. Retains a broad transfer axis from quiet standing through walking to vigorous jumping. Effort, execution speed and individual technique can overlap across classes; intensity alone is not a stair-direction discriminator.

operations.reason: cadence: G6 supports repetition rate in leg and body motion, allowing cycling and stepping to transfer from seen cyclic activities. Harmonics, short windows and unconstrained execution speed make exact ordinal boundaries uncertain; do not infer cadence solely from equipment or class identity.

Transfer is available from cycling and running. Sensor vibration and execution speed can alter apparent smoothness; this attribute cannot reliably distinguish the two static lying postures.

Preserves the principal recumbent-versus-upright cycling contrast, anchored by upright cycling and lying. Seat geometry and torso lean can vary, and isolated limb orientation must not substitute for global configuration.

Preserves transfer from regular exercise to cyclic unseen activities and from less structured basketball to elevator movement. Quiet signals can be predictable without periodic motion; short windows and pauses can obscure regularity.

operations.reason: bilateral_leg_synchrony: G14, G6 and G11 support assessing coordinated multiaxial leg motion and recurring timing in the available left and right leg IMUs. Concurrent bilateral propulsion and landing in two-leg jumping contrast with alternating stair steps, independently of impact strength; running and cycling anchor alternating motion, while rowing anchors coordinated bilateral leg action. This targets the close jumping–descending-stairs pair and jumping's weak seen coverage. Predictability is plausible for clear repeated movements, but hopping, asymmetric jumps, common torso-transmitted impacts and brief windows can obscure coordination. No precise inter-leg phase measurement or uniformly two-leg jumping is assumed.

semantic_redundancy_review: The ten attributes distinguish magnitude, repetition rate, sustained fluctuation, isolated impacts, mean posture, posture change, rotation, progression, predictability and bilateral coordination. Smoothness and impulsiveness are related but differ in sustained versus brief rapid changes; cadence and regularity distinguish rate from consistency. Bilateral leg synchrony concerns relative timing, not cadence, rotational magnitude or temporal regularity within an individual movement. No additional recumbency attribute duplicates posture inclination. No elevator-context or vertical-travel attribute is introduced because the listed capabilities do not guarantee its observability. Existing A1 prototype differences are not treated as measured evidence, and no class-level vectors are generated.
